files.description: Tests for the Photo Locations map: map renders with markers for GPS-tagged photos, clicking a marker opens the photo popup (and the closer hides it), the unnamed-only filter narrows and restores the feature set, shift-drag selection surfaces a reverse-geocoded name suggestion (route mocked), bulk-assigning a custom location name persists to the server, and the Clear-location-names action removes them again — restoring the seeded state. Serial + ordered: the two mutation tests run last.

testContext: The /locations page is a canvas-rendered OpenLayers map — markers are NOT DOM elements, so tests drive it through the API initMap exposes on window.PHOTO_ORGANIZER.locations.map ({map, vectorSource, selectedFeatures, updateSelectionPanel, applyFilter}). Wait for that global plus a 'rendercomplete' before doing pixel math (map.getPixelFromCoordinate(feature coords) + the #map bounding box gives real-mouse click targets). Located photos arrive embedded in the page (server renders locations | tojson into initMap); in the seeded sandbox only photo 14 (DSCN0010.jpg) has GPS, initially with location_name null. Interactions: click a marker -> #popup (an OL Overlay; hidden until positioned) shows img.popup-photo with data-fallback and a link to /media/view/{id} — NOTE the popup's first <a> is #popup-closer (href '#'), so scope link assertions to #popup-content. #filter-unnamed re-filters vectorSource in place. Shift+drag (ol DragBox, shiftKeyOnly) selects clusters and activates #selection-panel (.active class) with #mass-location-input + #mass-assign-btn posting to /locations/bulk-update; success shows a .notification.visible toast, clears the selection, and updates feature names in place. The panel also auto-POSTs the first cluster's centroid to /locations/reverse-geocode (external OSM Nominatim!) and, on success, inserts a .btn-recommended quick-assign button — ALWAYS mock this route in tests to stay offline-safe. Clearing names: POST /locations/bulk-update with {media_item_ids, clear: true} removes location names (clear must be boolean true; an empty location_name alone is still a 400 so a blank input can't wipe names) — the panel's '.btn-clear-names' button drives it and the toast uses locations:update.cleared. The mutation tests run LAST in serial order (assign 'Test Beach', then clear), so the suite restores the seeded unnamed state and re-runs stay green; the read-only tests still compute expectations from live vectorSource data.
explanation: 2026-07-01: Added locations_clear_location_names after the app gained a clear capability (POST /locations/bulk-update with clear: true + a 'Clear location names' panel button — previously names could never be removed, which forced one-way mutation tests). The clear test runs after the assign test and restores the seeded unnamed state, so re-runs and the unnamed-filter test see pristine data. Earlier in the day: initial generation with the canvas-map API approach and the mocked Nominatim reverse-geocode. All 6 tests pass twice in a row against a fresh sandbox.
